notice: The single authoritative run-lifecycle contract. The recorder drives transitions only through this table; the verifier loads the same file and reconstructs the archive state independently from persisted evidence. Prose: docs/v13i/LIFECYCLE.md.

CREATED.meaning: archive directory, empty ledger and initial manifest persisted; nothing fallible has run

PREFLIGHT.meaning: limits configured; the initial health read, when the server is observed, is in progress

READY.meaning: between draws: the next scheduled draw may start once its round health check and draw guard pass

HEALTH_CHECK.meaning: the round-boundary health read before the next draw is in progress

DRAW_ACTIVE.meaning: the draw guard passed for the next scheduled draw; it is executing, or has returned and is not yet committed

DRAW_RECORDED.meaning: the draw's row is committed to the authoritative ledger

CLEANUP.meaning: no further draw will start; pooled engine sessions are being released

FINALIZING.meaning: the FINALIZING marker is durable; final artifacts and the final manifest are being written

COMPLETE.meaning: every scheduled draw completed, no stop, cleanup succeeded, finalization durable

PARTIAL.meaning: finalized after a recorded stop or cleanup failure; only observed evidence is analysed

INVALID.meaning: assigned by the verifier to any archive that violates an invariant, is unfinalized, or cannot be read; never written by the recorder

events.begin_preflight: limits configured next; the initial health read follows when the server is observed
events.preflight_passed: initial health observation HEALTHY (or the server is not observed)
events.health_passed: round-boundary observation HEALTHY and the server signature unchanged
events.commit_draw: the row for the active draw is durable in draws.json
events.continue: the committed row completed and draws remain
events.schedule_done: the committed row completed and it was the last scheduled draw
events.stop: a stop is recorded (health, server_change, a guard halt, or a driver/operator exception)
events.cleanup_failed: pooled session release raised; recorded separately from any primary stop
events.finalize_complete: final manifest written as COMPLETE under the FINALIZING marker
events.finalize_partial: final manifest written as PARTIAL under the FINALIZING marker

illegalTransitions: every (from, event) pair not listed above, every transition out of COMPLETE or PARTIAL, any transition into INVALID, and any unknown state or event name: the recorder refuses it and the verifier classifies the archive INVALID (L14)

health.requires: the state's health check has a non-HEALTHY observation; failure null; request GET /health

server_change.requires: HEALTHY round observation whose server signature differs from the initial signature

wall_clock.requires: READY: draw-guard halt evidence (stage draw_start); DRAW_RECORDED: the committed row is interrupted with this halt

draw_call_limit.requires: the committed row is interrupted with this halt (stage request_start)

call_budget.requires: the committed row is interrupted with this halt (stage request_start)

transport.requires: the committed row is interrupted with this halt (stage request_start)

driver.requires: failure {type,message} with type other than KeyboardInterrupt; DRAW_ACTIVE requires the aborted artifact for the active draw; DRAW_RECORDED requires the committed row to be completed; CLEANUP only through cleanup_failed with no earlier stop

operator.requires: as driver, with failure type KeyboardInterrupt

abortedDraw.note: An aborted draw is the next scheduled draw, never a ledger row. failureStage determines the admissible initialization status and evidence; cleanupFailure is admissible only beside a different primary failure.

draw_unrecorded.meaning: the draw had been entered but raised without its own aborted evidence; nothing is reconstructed or invented

workflow.reconstruction: transport replay when the last recorded call failed without a body; otherwise UNVERIFIED

engine_close.cleanupFailure: forbidden (the close failure is the primary failure)

health.bodyRule: bytes over maxBodyBytes: oversized_body; not strict UTF-8: non_utf8_body; not JSON: invalid_json; not an object: not_an_object; an object with a key named error and status "healthy": contradictory_body; status not a non-empty string: missing_status; status "healthy": healthy; any other status: unhealthy_status

os_error.note: any other OSError subclass, by class; READ_FAILED either way

health.readFailureRule: categories are assigned by exception class (isinstance), never by message text; a URLError is categorised by its reason's class when that class is listed, otherwise url_error; every read failure has outcome READ_FAILED, an exception {type, reasonType}, no parsed body, and cause UNVERIFIED
health.contradiction: an observation whose recorded category, outcome, exception and body disagree (for example HEALTHY with an exception, or a body that re-classifies differently) is INVALID evidence (L07); it is never HEALTHY
health.noInvention: an interrupted read records no observation, only the attempted request; no response is ever substituted

healthSchedule: ordinary runs observe the server (serverObserved true); only an explicitly checked record-only fixture may leave it unobserved. When the server is observed: one read in PREFLIGHT, then one read in HEALTH_CHECK before schedule[i] whenever i == 0 or (model, draw round) differs from schedule[i-1]; none otherwise

artifacts.run.json: manifest: identities, claimed state, journal, counters, health checks, stop, failure event, cleanup, finalization
artifacts.draws.json: authoritative ledger: the committed rows (completed or interrupted), schedule prefix, atomic
artifacts.server-before.json: the full initial server state; required iff the server is observed and the initial read returned
artifacts.aborted-draw.json: required iff the stop is from DRAW_ACTIVE
artifacts.failure-event.json: required iff a stop exists; equal to run.failureEvent
artifacts.FINALIZING: marker present from the start of finalization until every final write and directory sync succeeded; its presence makes the archive INVALID

counters.drawInterrupted: seq of the interrupted ledger row, or null
counters.drawAborted: seq of the aborted artifact, or null
counters.modelCalls: recorded model exchanges in ledger rows plus the aborted artifact, failed attempts included
counters.healthChecks: recorded health checks, interrupted reads included

timestamps.format: UTC RFC 3339: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z, a valid calendar time
timestamps.order: run.started <= journal timestamps (non-decreasing) <= run.ended; run.ended equals the finalize transition; each observation started <= ended, inside its health-check interval; failureEvent.timestamp equals the stop transition; each draw's call times non-decreasing inside its begin_draw..commit/stop interval
timestamps.provenance: run.provenance.timestamps is SYSTEM_UTC for ordinary runs or SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE for reproducible record-only fixtures; the verifier refuses SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE unless explicitly asked to check a fixture
timestamps.replay: timestamps are metadata; deterministic draw replay identities exclude them; a missing timestamp is never inferred

interrupts.operatorSignal: SIGINT is deferred everywhere except inside interruptible regions (health read, draw execution, session release), and even there when it is handled in the recorder's own frame before the external call starts or after it returned; a deferred interrupt is raised at the next transition boundary before the run stops, and ignored for control once the run has stopped (it cannot undo or corrupt finalization)
interrupts.handled: an exception or interrupt outside persistence and outside the stop/cleanup/finalization sequence records stop driver/operator at the current state after reconciling the committed ledger
interrupts.reconciliation: before recording a stop from DRAW_ACTIVE the recorder commits a draw that had already returned, and records commit_draw (reconciled) for a row already durable in draws.json; it never invents an aborted artifact for a completed draw, nor a row that was not returned
interrupts.failClosed: a failure of any persistence operation, and any exception inside the stop/cleanup/finalization sequence other than the session release itself, propagates as a recording failure; the archive stays unfinalized (or keeps its FINALIZING marker) and is INVALID

steps: write FINALIZING marker (file and directory sync)
write failure-event.json when a stop exists
write run.json in its terminal state with SHA-256 of every archive file
finalization.rule: COMPLETE or PARTIAL is reported only after every step succeeded; if the final directory sync fails after the marker is removed the recorder restores the marker before failing
finalization.limits: atomic same-directory replacement per file and fsync where supported; no multi-file transaction, power-loss or filesystem-ordering guarantee is claimed

kinds.keyboard: KeyboardInterrupt raised at the point (an interrupt that is not deferred)
kinds.transport: a genuine transport failure: health read -> connection refused classified by the probe; model call -> failed exchange without a response
kinds.guard_halt: the run clock passes the wall-clock stop at the draw guard

persist:manifest.context: every transition checkpoint, identified by its event

expected.NO_ARCHIVE: fault before the initial manifest is durable: the recorder raises a recording failure; no run.json exists; the verifier classifies INVALID
expected.FAIL_CLOSED: persistence fault, or any fault inside the stop/cleanup/finalization sequence other than the session release: the recorder raises a recording failure; the archive is unfinalized or keeps its marker; the verifier classifies INVALID
expected.HANDLED: exception -> stop driver, keyboard -> stop operator, recorded at the state current at the fault; PARTIAL; completed draws = rows durable in draws.json plus a returned uncommitted draw
expected.HEALTH_STOP: transport fault during a health read: stop health with a READ_FAILED observation; PARTIAL
expected.GUARD_STOP: guard_halt: stop wall_clock at READY; PARTIAL
expected.CLEANUP_FAILED: fault during the session release: cleanup FAILED; any earlier stop is kept as primary, otherwise stop driver/operator at CLEANUP; PARTIAL
expected.WORKFLOW_EVIDENCE: model transport failure: a recorded failed exchange inside the draw; the lifecycle outcome is the base scenario's unless a guard halt follows from the recorded evidence

expectedRule.when: fault kind persistence, or phase in a persist/unlink operation other than before/after
fault inside the stop/cleanup/finalization sequence (stop recorded or state CLEANUP/FINALIZING) and not session_cleanup.during

L01.name: schedule prefix
L01.rule: ledger rows are schedule[0:n] in order with exact identities, each once; only the last may be interrupted; an aborted draw is schedule[n]

L02.name: completed evidence
L02.rule: every completed row has the complete draw/v4 evidence: record, batches, exact submitted representation and hash, initial and final digests, engine log, calls, READY initialization, no failure or cleanupFailure

L03.name: draw conservation
L03.rule: drawsScheduled = drawsCompleted + [drawInterrupted] + [drawAborted] + drawsNotRun, each counter equal to the value derived from the artifacts

L04.name: model-call reconciliation
L04.rule: run and failure-event call counts equal recorded exchanges; per-call order, request and response hashes and metadata hold; per-draw and run totals within the protocol bounds; halt evidence equals the recorded counts and failure streak

L05.name: aborted is not completed
L05.rule: an aborted draw is never a ledger row, only the next scheduled draw, only after a stop from DRAW_ACTIVE, and has status aborted

L06.name: failure stage
L06.rule: the stop's code is admissible in the state it was recorded from; the failure event's state equals the journal's stop source; an aborted failureStage admits only its initialization status and evidence

L07.name: health evidence
L07.rule: health checks occur exactly as healthSchedule requires; every observation is internally consistent and re-classifies from its body or exception; passing transitions require HEALTHY; a health stop requires a non-HEALTHY observation; server-before.json equals the initial state

L08.name: cleanup distinguishable
L08.rule: cleanup has SUCCEEDED or FAILED plus a separate failure; a cleanup failure never replaces an earlier primary stop; a cleanup-created stop equals the cleanup failure

L09.name: no unresolved failure in COMPLETE
L09.rule: COMPLETE has no stop, failure event, aborted artifact, interrupted row, failed cleanup or non-HEALTHY observation

L10.name: COMPLETE coverage and finalization
L10.rule: COMPLETE requires every scheduled draw completed and the journal tail schedule_done, cleanup_succeeded, finalize_complete

L11.name: PARTIAL suppression
L11.rule: a PARTIAL analysis has no complete-run arm differences or pair summaries

L12.name: INVALID never passes
L12.rule: any violation classifies the archive INVALID and analysis refuses it

L13.name: timestamps
L13.rule: every required timestamp is present, valid and ordered as timestamps.order requires; synthetic provenance only for explicit fixtures

L14.name: unknown transitions fail closed
L14.rule: the journal starts with create, chains from/to exactly, uses only listed transitions and names, and ends in the claimed terminal state

L15.name: identity binding
L15.rule: run schema, driver, lifecycle identity and SHA-256, UUID run identity, protocol identity and hash, and schedule hash agree

L16.name: artifact set and hashes
L16.rule: the archive has exactly the artifacts its derived state requires, no FINALIZING marker or stray file, failure-event.json equal to run.failureEvent, and every finalization hash equal to the file bytes

L17.name: journal-ledger binding
L17.rule: begin_draw and commit_draw name the scheduled draws in order; each commit_draw carries the row's canonical SHA-256, status and call count

L18.name: no resume
L18.rule: resume is never; an existing run directory is never reused

L19.name: single consistent stop
L19.rule: at most one stop transition; run.stop, failureEvent.stop and the journal agree on code and state
